incidents.name: Legacy Pool collectInterestRepayment missing access control
incidents.notes: The deprecated 2020 Pool's collectInterestRepayment(address,uint256) had no access control and executed USDC.transferFrom(from, pool, amount) for any address still holding a standing approval, so the attacker deposited 1,000 USDC, pulled a legacy depositor's USDC into the pool to inflate the share price, and withdrew the inflated balance.

sources.ref: callTracer review: the attack tx calls the legacy Pool 0x0689aa22...4B43 with deposit(uint256) 0xb6b55f25, collectInterestRepayment(address,uint256) 0x64de8a07 against victim 0x526C7665C5dd9cD7102C6d42D407a0d9DC1e431d, then withdraw(uint256) 0x2e1a7d4d four times; the Pool is Goldfinch's own 'TransparentProxy' created 2020-09-25 by 0xc840b3e21ff0eba77468ad450d868d4362cf67fe (not the attacker). It stores its implementation outside the EIP-1967 slot and signals changes with a custom event 0x5570d70a...8296, which fired only three times (blocks 10929405, 10948041, 10953821, all in Sep 2020) and always resolves to the same implementation 0x7dbe30fde1eca6856806ff14fc456ec6791c73fe, with none after — so the deployment-based age is not overstated in practice

deployment-basis recheck (storage, not events): contrary to the earlier note, this TransparentProxy does keep its implementation in the EIP-1967 slot 0x360894a1...2bbc, and the exploit tx's three DELEGATECALLs from the Pool all go to 0x7dbe30fde1eca6856806ff14fc456ec6791c73fe, exactly the value that slot holds. eth_getStorageAt returns 0x7dbe30fde1eca6856806ff14fc456ec6791c73fe at the creation block 10929405, at the incident block 23924517 and at all 41 evenly spaced samples in between, and the proxy runtime is byte-identical at both ends, so the Sep-2020 custom events did not move the implementation. Deployment remains the correct basis; 1894.2 days.
